how_to_read: Fields beyond id/title/source: `buzz` = how many DISTINCT outlets carry the same story (corroboration). `seen` = the paper already ran this story on that date: pick it again ONLY if there is a genuinely new fact (a verdict, number, reversal), never for continued interest. `flags` = why a desk editor would be wary (press-release wording, company's own channel, roundup/opinion format, weak fit with the section): treat flagged items as guilty until the text proves a real event. `when` (opportunities) = the real deadline/event date. Analysis of a skeleton from Denmark, nicknamed “Rødhals Man”, hints that the individual lived through one of the most fundamental changes in human history: the transition from hunter-gathering to farming.
“What was it like to live through such a momentous transition, seeing the archipelago where your ancestors had fished being transformed by the arrival of a new group of people?” says Anders Fischer at the University of Gothenburg in Sweden.

Adding a dash of lemon juice to a dish is among a good cook’s many tricks, but exactly why sour tickles the taste buds has long been a mystery. Now scientists have uncovered the precise neurochemistry behind this age-old culinary tip.
